name: liquid H2O, practical salinity 35, at 298 K

source: the Ocean Optics Web Book's "Water" page, eq. 1 and Table 1, for Quan and Fry's coefficients (https://www.oceanopticsbook.info/view/optical-constituents-of-the-ocean/water, SHA-256 7191efa9e11f04c9edde4156f2ba70fda81ae06e44e1d2346a9f0f3f54c65a04, fetched 2026-10-14; the paper is closed, and Zhang, Hu and He 2009, Opt. licence: reduced values: omlc.org states no terms for its transcription beyond the site's copyright notice, and the measured values are Pope and Fry's (decision-r08-licences.md); Hale and Querry's from refractiveindex.info (CC0 1.0, M. N. Polyanskiy, Sci. Data 11, 94 (2024)). The cross-check's seven values are Mason, Cone and Fry's, cited as facts; WOPP v3's file states no terms of its own (it is kept in the GPL-3.0 acolite repository), and none of it is committed; Quan and Fry's coefficients cited as facts, read from the Web Book (CC BY)
reduction: n = water.json's n plus Quan and Fry's salinity terms, (n₁ + n₂T + n₃T²)S + n₆S ÷ λ at S = 35‰ and T = 25 °C: +0.00672 at 380 nm, +0.00639 at 550 nm and +0.00618 at 780 nm, to six significant figures. Quan and Fry fitted Austin and Halikas 1976's data from 400–700 nm (the Web Book), relative to air, so their salinity terms alone are added to water.json's own n rather than their equation taken whole: the two files differ by Quan and Fry's salinity effect, and this one follows water.json's n should it change. k = water.json's: sea salts leave pure water's visible absorption unchanged within measurement (Röttgers, McKee and Utschig 2014, Opt. Express 22, 25093, DOI 10.1364/OE.22.025093: the salinity coefficient not significantly different from zero below 500 nm, and −0.18% to +0.04% per g L⁻¹ over 400–2,660 nm); their absorption lies in the ultraviolet. Seawater's molecular scattering is not in the file
